title: Factors In Considering Underground Alignments for Cross Island MRT Line
what_it_is: Factors In Considering Underground Alignments for Cross Island MRT Line

sections.label: Cross Island Line alignment questions
sections.summary: MP asks about factors for underground alignments near the Central Catchment Nature Reserve, the Lornie Road alternative, and online access to the Environmental Impact Assessment report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what are the main factors taken into consideration when deciding on the possible underground alignments in the vicinity of the Central Catchment Nature Reserve (CCNR) for the Cross Island Line; (b) in view of the moderate environmental impact on the nature reserve for the alignment option that cuts beneath CCNR, whether the Ministry will consider the alternative alignment along Lornie Road which will allow the MRT line to serve more residents and commuters in that vicinity and also result in the protection of our nature reserve and primary forest; and (c) whether the Environmental Impact Assessment report that was recently published can be made available for viewing online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: It will link east to west, from Changi to Jurong, covering more than 50 kilometres with about 30 stations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Our preliminary estimate is that commuters from residential areas like Loyang, Pasir Ris, Hougang, Ang Mo Kio, Sin Ming, Bukit Timah, Clementi and West Coast will make at least 600,000 trips on the CRL every day.

sections.label: Two alignments near nature reserve
sections.summary: The Government is studying two possible alignments for the Cross Island Line in the vicinity of the Central Catchment Nature Reserve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Specific to the question raised by the Member, the Government is studying two possible alignments for CRL in the vicinity of the Central Catchment Nature Reserve (CCNR).

sections.label: Direct alignment under nature reserve
sections.summary: For the four-kilometre direct alignment option, two kilometres will be deep below the Central Catchment Nature Reserve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: For the four-kilometre direct alignment option, two kilometres will be deep below CCNR.

sections.label: Surface facilities and higher cost
sections.summary: This option requires surface ventilation shafts and facilities, could cost around $2 billion more, and could result in land acquisitions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Therefore, it will require ventilation shafts and facilities on the surface, whereas in the earlier option, because it is short enough, you do not have to build all those quite ugly exhaust ducts which you see at some of our road junctions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: This option could incur around $2 billion – $2,000 million – more in expenditure and could result in land acquisitions.

sections.label: Two more years of studies
sections.summary: All these studies and consultations may take two more years to complete.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: All these studies and consultations may take two more years to complete.

sections.label: Site investigation and public consultations
sections.summary: If allowed to proceed with site investigation, more public consultations will let the Land Transport Authority firm up answers on who is affected and costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: For the next leg of the studies, if we are allowed to proceed with the site investigation, we will be doing much more public consultations and that will allow us, the Land Transport Authority (LTA), to firm up on many of the answers to many of the questions that have yet to be answered, such as who are affected, how much will it cost and so on.

sections.label: Permission for site investigation EIA
sections.summary: Permission is sought from MND to proceed with site investigation needed for the EIA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: What we are seeking is permission, in this case, from MND, to allow us to proceed with the site investigation for which there is a necessity to do this EIA.

sections.label: MND decision and EIA Phase 2
sections.summary: MND will consider views and decide on site investigation; if allowed, Phase 2 of the EIA follows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I am quite sure MND will take all those views into consideration and decide whether they would allow the site investigation to proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: And if they do, we can then enter into Phase 2 of the EIA, which will study what are the tunnelling methods, what will be the impact of those construction works and the subsequent running of the train on the nature reserve and, more importantly, whether there are suitable mitigation measures.

sections.label: EIA versus total impact study
sections.summary: The EIA studies a short stretch of line, while the job is a total impact study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The EIA is just an environmental impact study on a short stretch of a line, but our job is to do a total impact study – the impact on the environment, the impact on taxpayers, the impact on the commuters.

sections.label: LTA calculation of extra time
sections.summary: LTA calculated that a longer route crossing the reserve takes six extra minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I asked LTA, "Is their estimation correct?" And they did a calculation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: They said, "No, not quite." The extra time taken to cross the reserve, if it takes a longer route, is six minutes.
